newsitem.title: USA: Crown denies race, sex discrimination charges.
newsitem.headline: Crown denies race, sex discrimination charges.

text.p: Crown Central Petroleum Corp. Tuesday denied allegations of racial and sexual discrimination contained in a class-action lawsuit filed Monday.
Crown, which is also facing a lawsuit on pollution charges and a 16-month labour dispute at a refinery, is the fifth U.S. oil firm in the past three years to be hit with a discrimination suit.
"We feel we are very proud of our minority programmes here and feel the charges are groundless and without credibility in any form," company spokesman Joe Coale said.

Lawyers on behalf of more than 200 union and non-union female and African-American employees filed the discrimination suit against the Baltimore-based company in U.S. District Court in Beaumont, Texas, on Monday.

The suit alleges that supervisors at two of Crown's refineries denied African-American and female workers equal pay and promotions and continually circulated racist and sexually explicit cartoons and handbills.
"We have no reason to believe that this is factual and it's the first time (the handbills) have been brought to our attention," said Coale.
"Blacks and women hold prominent operating positions in our company and on our board," Coale added.
Discrimination suits have also been filed against Texaco Inc., Shell Oil, Pennzoil Co. and Coastal Corp.
Texaco settled its widely-publicised suit last March.

The workers at Crown are being represented by Cohen, Milstein, Hausfeld and Toll, which was involved in the Texaco case, as well as the firm Provost and Umphrey. Both firms are base in Washington D.C.
Crown's class A stock rose 12.5 cents to $14.75 on the American Stock Exchange shortly before midday.
